exposure: Maternal upper-body flexibility (assessed via Back-scratch test)
cohort: 157 pregnant women from the GESTAFIT Project.
finding: Lower maternal upper-body flexibility at 16 gestational weeks was associated with a significantly increased odds of requiring oxytocin administration during labor and undergoing a caesarean section.
mod_finding: Women with lower flexibility at 16 gestational weeks had a ~4 times greater odds ratio of having a caesarean section compared to a vaginal birth.
followup_time: Until birth (outcomes of labor and delivery)
